provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The emitted program works directly on the grid as shown. Colour roles are fixed as constants from the palette: background = palette[0], marker = palette[2], output canvas = palette[3]. The shape is every cell that is neither background nor marker. The marker line always sits strictly outside one edge of the shape's bounding box. The program checks right, left, below and above in visible coordinates and uses that edge as the mirror line. Right gives x -> 2*xmax+1-x, left gives x -> 2*xmin-1-x, and rows work the same way for below and above. It then paints the shape and its in-bounds reflection on the canvas colour. The reflection overwrites where the marker was. Because the side is found from the pixels, any rotation or reflection of the scene simply changes which edge is detected; no normalisation wrapper is needed. Rectangular grids are supported because H and W are read from the input. d4 is not needed: the side is already random in the original generator, so it cannot be specialised in advance.
draft_notes.limitations: This assumes the constructor's domain: exactly one shape colour (not background, marker or canvas colour) and a marker strictly beyond one bounding-box edge. If those assumptions break, a nearest-edge fallback heuristic is used. Reflected cells that fall outside the grid are clipped, which the generator never produces. The demonstrations are not used. The fixtures agree with this uniform rule. I have not run any tests.
